question.problem:
Find the vector $x$, if $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\},$ and  

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

current_example.problem:
Find the vector $\mathbf{x}$ if $\,\mathcal{B}=\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \},$ and
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274696/assets/faebc67c90eaf54dae31bf28f6e9d854b62e4ed03e09d94ebe8997af13c5e682.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
We know that any vector in  $\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2 \}$ has the form

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $x_1$ and $x_2$ are the coordinates relative to the basis $\,\mathcal{B}.$ Since we are told that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14274696/assets/c22f745d005bc781fc6cc4727ad154eebb927a72d14c5ffc6ac20ed9ba3740a9.svg) we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={{(-1)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
